title: GitLab CI: Pipelines, Jobs, and Runners
intro: The earlier CI/CD tutorials used GitHub Actions. GitLab CI is the other system you're most likely to meet, especially where code is self-hosted. The ideas map across: a .gitlab-ci.yml file, stages that run in order, jobs within a stage that run in parallel, and runners that execute them. You're in a repository with the glab CLI authenticated.

steps.fake_output:
Validating...
.gitlab-ci.yml is invalid

jobs:deploy config contains unknown keys: enviroment
steps.explanation: The deploy job has a misspelled key: 'enviroment'.
steps.why: The lint runs on GitLab's server with the real parser, so it also resolves 'include:' files and templates, which a local YAML check can't. A typo in a key is the common failure, and without linting you find out from a pipeline that fails to start, after the push.

steps.prompt: The typo is fixed and pushed. Check the status of the pipeline for the current branch.
steps.fake_output:
(success) • 01m 12s	test		unit
(success) • 00m 41s	test		lint
(failed)  • 02m 03s	build		image
(skipped)		deploy		production

https://gitlab.example.com/shop/api/-/pipelines/88120
SHA: a1f9c3e2
Pipeline state: failed
steps.explanation: Both test jobs passed in parallel; the build job failed, so deploy was skipped.
steps.why: Stages run in order and a failed stage stops the ones after it. Jobs in the same stage run together. So 'skipped' on deploy isn't a second problem, just a consequence. 'needs:' lets a job start as soon as its named dependencies finish, ignoring stage order, which is how large pipelines are made faster.

steps.prompt: Read the log of the failed job, named image.
steps.fake_output:
$ docker build -t $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA .
ERROR: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running?
Cleaning up project directory and file based variables
ERROR: Job failed: exit code 1
steps.explanation: The job can't reach a Docker daemon: it's running inside a container that has none.
steps.why: Jobs on a Docker-executor runner run inside a plain container. To build images you either add a 'docker:dind' service to the job, or, better, use a daemonless builder such as Kaniko or BuildKit's rootless mode. Docker-in-Docker needs a privileged runner, which gives every job on it root on the host; avoid that on shared runners.

steps.prompt: The job now uses a daemonless builder. Re-run just that job without a new commit.
steps.explanation: Only the failed job runs again; the test results are reused.
steps.why: Retry is for transient failures and for fixes outside the repository, such as a runner or a variable. If a retry passes with no change, the job is flaky and that deserves a ticket, not a habit: teams that retry by reflex stop noticing real failures.

steps.prompt: On the runner host, list the runners registered in its configuration.
steps.fake_output:
Runtime platform  arch=amd64 os=linux version=17.4.0
Listing configured runners  ConfigFile=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
docker-large  Executor=docker Token=glrt-t1_examp URL=https://gitlab.example.com
docker-small  Executor=docker Token=glrt-t1_exam2 URL=https://gitlab.example.com
steps.explanation: Two runners on this host, both using the Docker executor.
steps.why: A runner is an agent that polls GitLab for jobs; nothing connects inward to it, which makes runners easy to place inside private networks. Jobs choose runners by tags. A job whose tags match no online runner waits as 'pending' for ever, which is the most common GitLab CI support question (cicd-incident-007). 'gitlab-runner verify' checks each runner can still authenticate.

steps.prompt:
A deploy job should run only on the main branch and wait for a person to press a button. In .gitlab-ci.yml, which is the right way to express that?
  a) only: [main] together with a sleep command
  b) rules with a condition on $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main" and when: manual, plus an environment name
  c) A separate repository for deploys
  d) Comment the job out until needed
Type the letter.
steps.fake_output:
deploy:
  stage: deploy
  environment: production
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
      when: manual
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh
steps.hint: 'rules' replaced 'only/except', and 'when: manual' adds the button.
steps.explanation: rules decide whether the job exists in a pipeline; when: manual makes it wait.
steps.why: 'environment: production' is more than a label: GitLab records each deployment against it, can restrict who may run jobs for it (protected environments), and offers rollback to a previous deployment. Combined with protected branches and protected variables, it's what stops a job on someone's feature branch reading the production credentials.
